body:
I am for the 'AND' rather than 'OR' approach... of keeping the existing EVM running, but not viewing transaction fees as the only source of income...
This is because by rejecting smart contracts, the underlying value proposition of Edgeware would be diminished, which would likely cause a run ... if parallel revenue streams were established before that, perhaps not so much. 
I do see the potential for a DAO somewhat like Consensys or MetaCartel that is able to unite the various related factions in the substrate eco-system... but it does seem a bit risky, even if it would hedge against the EVM exploitation risk.

I'm not sure that we will have a clear answer on this quickly, but it's still a good poll and I'm glad we are discussing it.

---

Personally, I'd like to see this discussion settle out before doing any more core dev work. At the very least, I want to see a coherent political philosophy of Edgeware:

- Community of people with shared values and intentions, that should aim for 1-person-1-vote representation **(my thread)**
- We should be more decentralized, and not have any technical committee, which means core dev entities work independently **(moon)**
- Whatever is voted through goes **(Rich)**


So we're starting to end up at 'hardcore Substrate based governance' - close to 'code is law', where EDG is increasingly run by an anon community.

Which is fine, but it's different than the vision that Commonwealth has been working towards.

I'm not ready to propose anything now. I think some more time will help reveal whether we should support EVM in a limited capacity. As for myself, I'm narrowing down my focus, and have left most tech support channels and am only in the Discord now.

It would not be hard to get us onto a cleaner version of Substrate 3.0.0. But I do not want to be caught unprepared if the network halts, and it is doubly problematic if there are tokens at stake or our governance bodies are capricious or unresponsive. Which they are right now.

If other devs feel like they want to jump in, that'd be great too.

---

@Rich - All the pallet-based projects above require technical talent from the EDG side...do we have that?

I heard you had other proposals for apps to come to Edgeware that you were helping to workshop; maybe sharing some of those would help.

Sorry [@raymondz](/edgeware/account/mae7JWE1EEMLcno2ZSB8dahwPqVPEyh8zik6dgNpQTvvucq) - i'd meant to respond to the 1p1v point in your [original post](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/2140-a-note-on-edgeware-governance-clarity-shared-values-and-a-1p1v-committee) but things moved on, however I do support governance that includes both meritocratic and coin-weighted elements. 

In the end, there is a lot of talk, but proposals lock in **doers **and it is this talent that we need to reach, educate and inspire. since retaining them will be how we move things forward. 

People/groups who put forward proposals that are agreed by the community and delivered as proposed, or at least completed to the satifaction of peers should a review / change of direction be needed. 

In this model, 1p1v moves us towards a **digital cooperative model**, pooling and managing shared resources.

On the other two points:

- We should be more decentralized, and not have any technical committee, which means core dev entities work independently **(moon)**


These devs should put forward proposals and would therefore become part of a 1p1v digital cooperative. 

- Whatever is voted through goes 


Again relates to the 1p1v direction. **We are what we vote. **

It's the only way we can conclude debates in a meaningful way and lock in the will of the collective. 

We can debate general metrics, in the end I think we are so early in this experiment and a small collective, that we should not lock in too fine grained metrics or KPIs, instead trusting to the fact that the proposals build on and extend existing capabilities and offer something interesting or exciting people would like to see happen...

Hopefully this would drive:

- **Participation in the DAO **
- **comments, discussions, proposals**
- **Governance engagement **
- **voting on proposals / referenda / upgrades**
- **Build out of Edgeware's capabilities **
- **infrastructure / tooling / apps / products / media **

Sorry missed this [@raymondz](/edgeware/account/mae7JWE1EEMLcno2ZSB8dahwPqVPEyh8zik6dgNpQTvvucq) 
> @Rich - All the pallet-based projects above require technical talent from the EDG side...do we have that? 
Thats what I've been working on, we are definitely light here, but it's kind of chicken and egg... we need a direction / some proposals that push us forward and can excite devs, but that also demonstrate where we have holes in our talent.

This then makes it easier to focus on the people we need to bring in and then like the arrival of [@Ramsey](/edgeware/account/k44nJ5yAhFz3XHGeTPuKvegJ4GD1YCSVaPc7wj4miVL6epN) we add to our collective experience. 

> I heard you had other proposals for apps to come to Edgeware that you were helping to workshop; maybe sharing some of those would help. 

Yes, will be coming over next few weeks and will definitely be a good way to fill out roles / add expertise.

A 1p1v DAO co-op with all Edgeware proposers would be cool.

I don't know how it could be used (it seems on-chain governance wouldn't generally follow its direction) but it could lead to something interesting down the line. Fun to build + riff on.

IMO imagining new incentive designs, complex modeling processes, or anything that engages our bureaucracy and takes months is a failing choice, we have issues _now. _

re: the amount. That's the amount that I think would help secure a _competitive_ maintaining team.  I've been saying for two months that I plan to offer strong incentives to core developers in council chat and otherwise.  **Let's not waste time being surprised, and instead focus on the right offer. **

> There should be AND instead of OR. We need to do both "Fund a small dev team to maintain the robust smart contract chain status" and also "Focus on community benefits funding and the DAO functionality."

How much? Let's just start there. What is this worth to you? 

> **None of the agency members was made aware of this in detail. Thus I believe this doesn't truly represent "Agency's potential paths".**

I don't consult all members in helping determine strategy, per the agency proposal. Staff and members are of course free to disagree, but I continue to set direction for the org. 

If we want to keep smart contracts, then let's do it right, and truly contribute to an ecosystem like a leader, but it's going to cost the public some coin, and we should evaluate what that # is, if you think 15%-30% is too much, what is a good #?  **If you want smart contracts, you should answer this Q; EDG has no core developer at this time. **

I wholeheartedly reject bounties-based core development for our experimental tech. We need someone (ideally 2-5) on deck to be a good smart contracts platform.

If instead, we are unwilling to incentivize this work, we may want to focus on what we do well right now, we should disclaim our contracting modules as being unreliable, or remove them. It's an honorable path and opens other doors like the use of palettes as a priority, and doubles down on DAO operations, to Ramsey's point.
Edgeware is an ashram for founders to come and meditate on blockchain, sweep a few floors and get enlightened about building their own thing.

I voted for option 1 but the ONLY reason was that I invested into a Smart contract chain not DAO only chain...I do not agree to strictly separate this vote by introducing logical OR operator...so in essence Shankar's post is representing my opinion also.

Yikes indeed. 

I guess a good proposal should be marmite, apathy is often less useful than a truly split opinion but I also think that this reward is insanely high - to a point I wondered if you were serious?

If circulating supply is 6.5bn or so are you suggesting 1.9Bn (30%) vesting over a number of years?

To be clear i would support a budget for core maintenance but nothing like this. 

You've labelled this a proposal, but again we can't vote on this because its more a discussion point. We should vote on funding a bounty for core development maybe, or a specific proposal from a recruited maintainer, but I can't vote yes/no on this, as its doesn't capture any of the nuance per [@Shankar Warang](/edgeware/account/jA7pLH65zgRNA4UgwqHEWWRxTgg51wuAUgfzmZoYWM2dMVS)'s point.

body: we literally just voted a few weeks ago on "SimpleMajority: A Proposed Edgeware Governance Standard" :-)

That was a single, specific feature within our governance tools, it was a clear yes/no on a detail that we had informally agreed as a standard. 

This is clearly a bigger and more nuanced / complex subject.

I understand the point of the debate but right now it doesn't need to be either or with the extremes suggested. 

We are already operating majority DAO first... aka funding projects like Zien, that then utilise EVM and smart contracts.

On the other side, something like New Futures (comparable to Zien) is starting DAO first, before using pallets, and then Ink / WASM when it is ready...

We don't need a "core team" but rather a CTO and a junior developer to start with.
30-40% is a too massive amount and I have never seen even a single conventional project allocating this much of supply to a "core team".
Could you please elaborate on how you determined the new value i.e. 15-30%? This could massively go against our "fair distribution" trait.

**None of the agency members was made aware of this in detail. Thus I believe this doesn't truly represent "Agency's potential paths".**
Ideally, now that we have the DAO Financial Strategist team, they should be involved to do proper research and analysis for the dev team's incentivization structure.

There should be AND instead of OR. We need to do both "Fund a small dev team to maintain the robust smart contract chain status" and also "Focus on community benefits funding and the DAO functionality."
Gotta keep our 'experimental governance' chops somehow. ;p
